title: Sleep in peace
hookLine: the eleven blessings of metta, read whole

cards: Two in the morning, and the day is replaying: what they said, what you should have said. The last sutta of the week speaks to that hour.

It comes from the final book of the Numbered Sayings, the Book of Elevens, and it lists what happens to a person who practices loving-kindness, metta, steadily: developed, cultivated, made a vehicle and a foundation, the text says, well established and well undertaken.
There are eleven blessings, and today we read the whole list.

teach.b: Here they are, in order. One: you sleep easily. Two: you wake easily.
Three: you don't have bad dreams.
Four: you are dear to human beings. Five: you are dear to non-human beings. Six: the devas, the gods, protect you.
Seven: fire, poison and weapons don't touch you. Eight: your mind becomes concentrated quickly.

teach.h: A QUICK MIND, A BRIGHT FACE.
teach.b: Nine: your face is bright and clear.
Ten: you die unconfused. Eleven: if you go no further in this life, you are reborn in the Brahma world. Notice where the list starts: not with heaven, with sleep.
The first three blessings are about the night, where resentment and worry do their best work. A heart that's practiced goodwill has less to replay.
Then the list moves outward, to people, to unseen beings, to protection; then inward, to concentration and a clear face; and finally to the very end, dying without confusion.
A whole life, from tonight's pillow to the last breath.

Some of the blessings, like fire and poison not touching you, are read by some teachers literally, as the power of a mind full of kindness, and by others as describing a life that makes fewer enemies.
The text itself simply lists them. And it ties the week together: grudges removed, winds passing, less wanting, all of it makes for a quieter night.

how: In some Theravada communities the eleven blessings of metta are chanted in Pali, and metta meditation, wishing well to oneself and then widening circles of beings, is a common practice before sleep.

o: loving-kindness, a steady wish for others' good
a prayer asking the gods for protection
a quiet chant repeated to fall asleep

games.q: sleep in peace: tap the pairs.

s: the list of metta's blessings begins with heaven
it begins with sleep: sleeping easily, waking easily, no bad dreams.
there are eleven blessings in the list
it's in the Book of Elevens, the last book of the Numbered Sayings.
one blessing is being dear to non-human beings
dear to humans, and dear to non-humans too.

games.q: of the eleven blessings of metta, which comes first in the list?
games.why: sleep comes first. the list starts with tonight's pillow and ends with dying unconfused.

practice: Breathe slowly and wish yourself well in a few simple words, may I be well, may I rest; then someone you love; then someone neutral, a face you passed today; then, if you can, someone from this week's grudges.
Then everyone, everywhere, going to sleep tonight, the words getting softer as you go. You can do it now, or keep it for your pillow tonight.

wordCard.voice: metta. The Pali word for loving-kindness, the practice behind the eleven blessings in the Book of Elevens, a list that runs from an easy night to an unconfused death and beyond. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali metta: loving-kindness, goodwill; from mitta, friend. Sanskrit maitri.

carryVoice: Your line: wish one person well. Eleven blessings, and the first is a good night's sleep. A week done; sleep well.
